newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to buy Koenig Sporting Goods stores.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to buy Koenig Sporting Goods stores.

text.p: Retailer Woolworth Corp. said Monday it had agreed to buy stores from bankrupt Koenig Sporting Goods Inc. for about $10 million in cash.

Woolworth, which last month announced it will close its 400 "five-and-dime" stores due to competition from retailing giant Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and others, said it was buying Koenig's 27 stores in areas where its Champs Sports division did not have a presence.
The stores are in Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Buffalo, N.Y., it said.
Woolworth said it expects to convert the stores to its Champs Sports format.
The New York-based company said it has 540 Champs Sports stores in North America.
Koenig said it plans to exit the sporting goods business and resolve its financial obligations through a Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceeding.
The transaction is subject to Bankruptcy Court approval and other customary conditions.
Woolworth stock was unchanged at $25.875 in composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
